13:1: As for the discussion of the disconnected letters at the beginning of the surahs, it was mentioned at the beginning of Surah Al-Baqarah, and we mentioned that every surah that begins with these letters contains the victory of the Qur’an and clarification that its revelation from God is true, without doubt, uncertainty, or suspicion. For this reason, He said: These are the verses of the Book, meaning these are the verses of the Book, which is the Qur’an. It was also said: the Torah and the Gospel, as Mujahid and Qatadah said, and there is a view in it, rather it is far-fetched. Then He connected to that the connection of attributes, so He said: And that which has been revealed to you, meaning O Muhammad, from your Lord is the truth, a predicate whose subject preceded, which is His saying: And that which has been revealed to you from your Lord, this is the correct one that matches the interpretation of Mujahid and Qatadah. Ibn Jarir chose that the waw be extra or a conjunction of an attribute with an attribute, as we mentioned, and he cited as evidence the saying of the poet: To the venerable king, the son of the hero, and the lion of the battalion in the crowded place His saying: But most people do not believe is like his saying: And most people, even if you strive to do so, will not believe. That is, despite this clarification, clarity, and plainness, most of them do not believe because of the discord, stubbornness, and hypocrisy within them.
13:2: God Almighty tells us about the perfection of His power and the greatness of His authority, that He is the One by whose permission and command He raised the heavens without pillars, but by His permission, command and subjugation He raised them above the earth to a distance that cannot be reached or comprehended. The lowest heaven surrounds all of the earth and what is around it of water and air from all its sides, directions and corners, rising above it from every side equally, and the distance between it and the earth from every side is a journey of five hundred years, and its thickness in itself is a journey of five hundred years. Then the second heaven surrounds the lowest heaven and what it contains, and between them from the distance of the journey is five hundred years, and its thickness is five hundred years, and so on for the third, fourth, fifth, sixth and seventh heavens, as God Almighty said: God is He who created seven heavens and of the earth the like thereof verse. In the hadith: “The seven heavens and what is in them and what is between them in relation to the Kursi are like a ring thrown in a deserted land, and the Kursi in relation to the Glorious Throne is like that ring in that desert.” In another narration: And the Throne is only estimated by God, the Almighty and Majestic. It was reported from some scholars that the distance between the Throne and the Earth is a journey of fifty thousand years, and the distance between its two poles is a journey of fifty thousand years, and it is made of red ruby. His statement: Without pillars that you see it, was reported from Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Al-Hasan, Qatadah and more than one other that they said: It has pillars but they are not seen. Iyas bin Muawiyah said: The sky is above the earth like a dome, meaning without pillars. This is also narrated from Qatada, and this is what is appropriate to the context, and what is apparent from the Almighty’s saying: And He holds back the sky from falling upon the earth except by His permission. Based on this, His saying: You see it is an emphasis on the negation of that, meaning it is raised without pillars as you see it, and this is the most perfect in ability. And in the poetry of Umayyah bin Abi al-Salt, whose poetry believed, but whose heart disbelieved as mentioned in the hadith, and it is narrated from Zayd bin Amr bin Nufayl, may God be pleased with him: And you are the one who, out of your grace and mercy, sent a messenger to Moses, calling out I said to him: Go with Aaron and call to God Pharaoh, who was a tyrant. And say to him: Did you do this without a peg so that it became independent as it is? And say to him: Did you raise this without intention or did you build on that? And say to him: Did you make the middle of it lit up when the night comes to you? And say to him: Who sends the sun in the morning, so that whatever it touches of the earth becomes bright? And say to him: Who made the seed grow in the soil, so that the grass sways and grows from it? And his love comes out of his heads? In that are signs for whoever is aware. The Almighty’s saying: Then He established Himself on the Throne has been explained in Surat Al-A’raf, and that it passes as it came without any specification, likening, nullification, or representation. Exalted be God, far above. And His saying: And He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running for a specified term. It has been said that what is meant is that they run until they cease with the coming of the Hour, like His Almighty’s saying: And the sun runs to its resting place. It has also been said that what is meant is their resting place, which is under the Throne, which is adjacent to the belly of the Earth on the other side. For if they and all the other planets reach there, they will be the furthest thing from the Throne, because according to the correct view upon which the evidence is based, it is a dome adjacent to the world from this side, and it is not encompassing like the other spheres, because it has pillars and bearers who carry it, and this is not conceivable in a round sphere. This is clear to whoever ponders what has been reported in the verses and authentic hadiths. Praise and thanks be to God. He mentioned the sun and the moon because they are the most prominent of the seven planets, which are more noble and greater than the fixed ones. So if He has subjected these, then it is even more appropriate that the other planets should be included in the subjection, as He indicated in His Most High’s saying: Do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon, but prostrate to God, who created them, if it is Him that you worship. Although He made this clear in His saying: “And the sun, the moon, and the stars are subjected by His command. Unquestionably, His is the creation and the command. Blessed be God, Lord of the worlds.” And His saying: He details the signs that you may be certain of the meeting with your Lord. That is, He explains the signs and evidence indicating that there is no god but Him, and that He will restore creation if He wills, just as He began it.
13:3: When God Almighty mentioned the upper world, He began to mention His power, wisdom, and perfection of the lower world, saying: And it is He who spread out the earth, meaning He made it vast and extended in length and width, and anchored it with towering, lofty mountains, and caused rivers, streams, and springs to flow in it, to water the fruits He created in it of different colors, shapes, tastes, and scents, of every kind two mates, meaning two kinds of every kind, He causes the night to cover the day, meaning He made each of them seek the other with a persistent search, so when one goes, the other covers it, and when the other ends, the other comes, so He also acts in time as He acts in place and people, Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought, meaning in the favors of God, His wisdom, and His proofs. And His statement: And on the earth are adjacent tracts meaning lands that are adjacent to each other, although some are good and produce what benefits people and others are salty salt marshes that produce nothing. This is how it was narrated from Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Saeed bin Jubayr, Ad-Dahhak and others. This verse includes the difference in the colors of the parts of the earth, so this soil is red, this is white, this is yellow, this is black, this is stony, this is flat, this is sandy, this is thick, this is thin, and all are adjacent, so this is according to its description, and this is according to another description, so all of this is what indicates the chosen doer, there is no god but Him and no lord but Him. And His statement: And gardens of grapes and crops and palm trees may be a conjunction with gardens, in which case and crops and palm trees would be nominative. And it may be conjoined with grapes, in which case it would be genitive, and for this reason a group of imams read each of them. His saying: Two and not two. The two is the roots gathered in one place, such as the pomegranate, the fig, some palm trees, and the like. And not two is what is on one root, such as all trees. From this, a man’s paternal uncle was called his father’s twin, as came in the Sahih that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Umar: Did you not know that a man’s paternal uncle is his father’s twin? Sufyan al-Thawri and Shu’bah said on the authority of Abu Ishaq on the authority of al-Bara’, may God be pleased with him: The two is the palm trees on one root, and not two is the scattered ones. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, and others. And his saying: They are watered with one water, and We give some of them preference over others in eating. Al-A’mash said on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: And We give some of them preference over others in eating. He said: The date palm, the Persian date, the sweet, and the sour. Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi, who said: Hasan Gharib. That is, this difference in the types of fruits and crops in their shapes and colors, their tastes and smells, their leaves and flowers. This is extremely sweet, this is extremely sour, this is extremely bitter, this is tannic, this is sweet, this combines this and that, then it changes into another taste by the permission of God Almighty. This is yellow, this is red, this is white, this is black, and this is blue. Likewise, flowers, although they all derive from one nature, which is water, with the many differences that are not limited or controlled. In that are signs for whoever is aware, and this is one of the greatest indications of the Doer of Choice, who by His power differentiated between things and created them as He willed. For this reason, God Almighty said: Indeed in that are signs for a people who disbelieve. They understand.

13:5: God the Almighty says to His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And if you are amazed at the denial of these polytheists of the Resurrection, with what they witness of the signs of God the Almighty and His evidence in His creation that He is able to do whatever He wills, and with what they acknowledge that He began the creation of things and their being after they were nothing worth mentioning, then after this they deny His report that He will create the world a new creation, and they have acknowledged and witnessed what is more amazing than what they denied, so the wonder is their saying If we are dust, will we then be in a new creation? And every scholar and rational person knows that the creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of people, and that whoever began creation, the repetition is easier for Him, as God the Almighty says: Do they not see that God, who created the heavens and the earth and was not weary of their creation, is able to give life to the dead? Yes, He is over all things competent. Then He described the deniers with this and said: "Those are the ones who disbelieved in their Lord, and those are the ones in shackles in Their necks” meaning they will be dragged by it into the Fire and those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally meaning they will remain therein forever, they will not move from it or disappear.
13:6: The Almighty says: And they urge you meaning these deniers for the evil before the good meaning the punishment as He informed us about them in His statement: "And they said, 'O you to whom the message has been sent down, you are truly mad. If only you would not bring us the angels, if you should be of the truthful. We do not send down the angels except with the truth, and if they were not, they would not be reprieved.'" And the Almighty said: And they urge you for the punishment the two verses, and the Almighty said: A questioner asked about a punishment to come, and He said: Those who do not believe in it urge it on, but those who believe are fearful of it and know that it is the truth. "And they said, 'Our Lord, hasten for us our portion'" the verse, meaning our punishment and reckoning, as He said informing us about them: "And when they said, 'O God, if this is the truth from You'" the verse, so they were, due to the intensity of their denial, stubbornness, and disbelief, asking that the punishment of God be brought to them. The Almighty said: "And before them have passed examples" meaning We inflicted Our punishment on the previous nations and made them A lesson and a sermon for those who learn from them. Then the Almighty informed that if it were not for His forbearance and pardon, He would have hastened the punishment upon them, as He said: And if God were to punish people for what they have earned, He would not leave a living creature on the earth’s back. And the Almighty said in this noble verse: And indeed, your Lord is full of forgiveness for the people despite their wrongdoing. That is, He, the Almighty, is full of forgiveness, pardon, and concealment for the people, even though they wrong and sin by night and by day. Then He linked this ruling with being severe in punishment, so that hope and fear would be balanced, as the Almighty said: But if they deny you, then say, ‘Your Lord is full of vast mercy, and His punishment is not averted from the criminal people.’ And He said: Indeed, your Lord is swift in penalty, but indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful. And He said: Inform My servants that it is I who am the Forgiving, the Merciful, and that My punishment is the painful punishment. And similar verses that combine hope and fear. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Musa bin Ismail told us, Hammad told us, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, who said: When this verse was revealed, And indeed, your Lord is the Possessor of forgiveness for the people, despite their wrongdoing, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Were it not for God’s pardon and forgiveness, no one would enjoy life, and were it not for His threat and punishment, no one would be tired. Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir narrated in the biography of Al-Hasan bin Othman Abu Hassan Al-Ziyadi that he saw the Lord of Glory in a dream, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was standing before Him interceding for a man from his nation, so He said to him: Is it not enough for you that I revealed to you in Surat Al-Ra’d, And indeed, your Lord is the Possessor of forgiveness for the people, despite their wrongdoing, he said: Then I woke up.
13:7: God the Almighty says, informing us about the polytheists that they say in disbelief and stubbornness: Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord as the former ones were sent, as they were stubborn with him to make for them Safa into gold, and to remove the mountains from them, and to replace them with meadows and rivers, God the Almighty says: And nothing prevented Us from sending the signs except that the former ones denied them the verse, God the Almighty says: You are only a warner meaning that you are only responsible for conveying the message of God that He has commanded you, You are not responsible for guiding them, but God guides whom He wills and His statement: And for every people is a guide Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: meaning for every people is a caller. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse: God the Almighty says: You, O Muhammad, are a warner, and I am the guide of every people, and this is what Mujahid, Saeed bin Jubayr, Ad-Dahhak and others said. On the authority of Mujahid: And for every people there is a guide, meaning a prophet, like His statement: And there was no nation but that a warner had passed among them, and this is what Qatada and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said. Abu Salih and Yahya ibn Rafi’ said: And for every people there is a guide, meaning a leader. Abu al-Aaliyah said: The guide is the leader, the leader is the imam, and the imam is the action. On the authority of Ikrimah and Abu al-Dhaha: For every people there is a guide, they said: He is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Malik said: And for every people there is a guide, who calls them to God Almighty. Abu Ja`far bin Jarir said: Ahmad bin Yahya al-Sufi told us, al-Hasan bin al-Husayn al-Ansari told us, Mu`adh bin Muslim told us, al-Harawi told us, on the authority of `Ata` bin al-Sa`ib, on the authority of Sa`id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: When the verse, You are only a warner, and for every people there is a guide, was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, placed his hands on his chest and said, I am the warner, and for every people there is a guide, and he pointed with his hand to Ali’s shoulder and said, You are the guide, O Ali, through you the rightly guided ones after me are guided. This hadith is very objectionable. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin al-Husayn told us, `Uthman bin Abi Shaybah told us, al-Muttalib bin Ziyad told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, on the authority of `Abd al-Khayr, on the authority of Ali, And for every people there is a guide, he said: The guide is a man from Banu Hashim. Al-Junayd said: He is Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Something similar was narrated on the authority of Ibn `Abbas in one of the narrations and on the authority of Abu Ja`far Muhammad bin Ali.
13:8: The Almighty informs about His complete knowledge that nothing is hidden from Him, and that He encompasses what pregnant women carry from all female animals, as the Almighty said: And He knows what is in the wombs meaning what they carry of male or female, or good or bad, or happy or miserable, or long-lived or short-lived, as the Almighty said: He knows you best when He created you from the earth and when you were fetuses verse, and the Almighty said: He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation, in three darknesses meaning He created you, one stage after another, as the Almighty said: “And We have certainly created man from an extract of clay. Then We placed him as a sperm-drop in a firm lodging. Then We made the sperm-drop into a clot, then We made the clot into a lump of flesh, then We made the lump of flesh into bones, then We clothed the bones with flesh, then We developed him into another creation. So blessed be God, the best of creators.” And in the two Sahihs on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The creation of one of you is gathered together in his mother’s womb. Forty days, then it becomes a clot for a similar period, then it becomes a lump of flesh for a similar period, then God sends an angel to him who is commanded with four words: to write down his provision, his lifespan, his deeds, and whether he will be wretched or happy.” And in another hadith, The angel says, ‘O Lord, am I male or female? O Lord, am I wretched or happy? What is the provision? What is the lifespan?’ God says, and the angel writes. Al-Bukhari said: Ibrahim bin Al-Mundhir narrated to us, Ma’n narrated to us, Malik narrated to us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Dinar, on the authority of Ibn Umar, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The keys of the unseen are five, and none knows them but God: None knows what will happen tomorrow but God, and none knows what the wombs conceal but God, and none knows when the rain will come but God, and no soul knows in what land it will die, and none knows when the Hour will come but God.” Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And the wombs conceal means the miscarriage, and and they conceal means: the womb does not increase in pregnancy beyond what it has concealed until it gives birth to it completely. This is because some women carry their pregnancy for ten months, and some for nine months, and some for more, and some for less. This is the diminishing and increasing that God, the Most High, mentioned, and all of that is by His knowledge, the Most High. Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And what the wombs decrease or increase, he said: What they decrease from nine and what they increase. Ad-Dahhak said: My mother gave birth to me and she carried me in her womb for two years, and she gave birth to me and my two front teeth had grown. Ibn Jurayj said on the authority of Jamilah bint Saad on the authority of Aisha who said: Pregnancy does not last more than two years, the amount of time it takes for the shadow of a spindle to move. Mujahid said: And what the wombs decrease or increase, he said: What she sees of blood during her pregnancy, and what she increases beyond nine months. This is what Atiyah Al-Awfi, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Qatadah and Ad-Dahhak said. Mujahid also said: If a woman sees blood for less than nine, it increases beyond nine like the days of menstruation. This was said by Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubair and Ibn Zayd. Mujahid also said: And what the wombs decrease or increase is the shedding of blood until the child is lost, and what she increases if the woman does not shed blood, the child is complete and great. Makhool said: The fetus in its mother’s womb does not ask, nor does it grieve, nor does it feel sad. Rather, its sustenance comes to it in its mother’s womb from her menstrual blood. Hence, a pregnant woman does not menstruate. When it falls to the ground, it cries out, and its cries are a sign of its astonishment at its place. When its navel is cut, God transfers its sustenance to its mother’s breasts so that it does not grieve, nor ask, nor feel sad. Then it becomes a child who takes something with his hand and eats it. When it reaches maturity, it says: It is death or murder. How can I have sustenance? Makhool says: Woe to you! It nourished you while you were in your mother’s womb and you were a small child. Then, when you grow up and become mature and sensible, you say: It is death or murder. How can I have sustenance? Then Makhool recited: God knows what every female carries. Qatada said: And everything with Him has a measured term, meaning by a set time. He preserved the provisions and lives of His creation, and set a known term for that. In the authentic hadith, one of the daughters of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent word to him that her son was dying, and she would like him to be present with him. So he sent word to her saying: To God belongs what He takes and to Him belongs what He gives, and everything with Him has a set term, so command her to be patient and seek reward. The hadith in full. And His statement: Knower of the unseen and the seen, meaning He knows everything that His servants see and everything that is hidden from them, and nothing of it is hidden from Him. The Great is greater than everything, The Most High meaning over everything. He has encompassed all things in knowledge, and He has subdued all things, so necks have submitted to Him and the servants have submitted to Him willingly or unwillingly.

In the authentic hadith, one of the daughters of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent word to him that her son was dying, and she would like him to be present with him. So he sent word to her saying: To God belongs what He takes and to Him belongs what He gives, and everything with Him has a set term, so command her to be patient and seek reward. The hadith in full. And His statement: Knower of the unseen and the seen, meaning He knows everything that His servants see and everything that is hidden from them, and nothing of it is hidden from Him. The Great is greater than everything, The Most High meaning over everything. He has encompassed all things in knowledge, and He has subdued all things, so necks have submitted to Him and the servants have submitted to Him willingly or unwillingly.
13:10: The Almighty informs us about His knowledge encompassing all of His creation, and that whether they conceal their words or declare them openly, He hears them and nothing is hidden from Him, as in His saying: And if you speak aloud, then indeed He knows the secret and what is even more hidden, and He said: And He knows what you conceal and what you declare, Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: Glory be to Him whose hearing encompasses all sounds. By God, the woman who argued with you about her husband came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I was in the corner of the house, and some of her words were hidden from me, so God revealed: “God has heard the statement of the one who argues with you concerning her husband and directs a complaint to God. And God hears your dialogue. Indeed, God is Hearing and Seeing.” And His saying: And whoever hides by night, meaning hiding in the depths of his house in the darkness of the night, and travels by day, meaning appearing and walking in the whiteness and brightness of the day, then both of them are in God’s knowledge equally, as in His saying: Except when they cover themselves with their garments, the verse. And the Almighty said: “And you are not engaged in any affair, nor do you recite from it any Qur’an, nor do you do any deed, but We are witnesses over you when you are engaged in it. And not an atom’s weight is hidden from your Lord, whether on earth or in heaven, nor anything smaller than that or larger, but that it is in a clear register.” And His saying: He has angels before him and behind him, guarding him by the command of God means that the servant has angels who take turns guarding him, guarding him by night and guarding him by day, guarding him from evils and accidents, just as other angels take turns guarding his deeds, whether good or evil, angels by night and angels by day. So two on the right and left write down the deeds, the one on the right writes down the good deeds, and the one on the left writes down the bad deeds, and two other angels guard and guard him, one behind him and another in front of him, so he is between four angels by day and four angels by night, instead of two guardians and two writers, as came in the Sahih: “Angels take turns guarding you by night and angels by day, and they gather at the dawn prayer and the afternoon prayer, and those who spent the night among you ascend to Him, and He asks them, and He is the most knowing of you: How did you leave My servants? They say: We came to them while they were praying, and we left them while they were praying.” In another hadith: There are those with you who will not leave you except when relieving oneself and having sexual intercourse, so be modest with them and honor them. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: He has angels before him and behind him who guard him by the command of God. The angels from God are the angels. Ikrimah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: They guard him by the command of God. He said: Angels guard him before him and behind him, so when the decree of God comes, they leave him. Mujahid said: There is no servant but that he has an angel assigned to him, who guards him in his sleep and when he is awake from the jinn, humans, and vermin, so nothing of them comes to him wanting him, except that the angel says to him, Behind you, except something that God has permitted, so it befalls him. Al-Thawri said on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: He has guardians before him and behind him, he said: That is a king from the kings of this world, he has guards behind him, guards behind him. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He has guardians before him and behind him, meaning the guardian of Satan who has guards over him. Ikrimah said in its interpretation: These are the princes who are guarded before him and behind him. Ad-Dahhak said about the verse: He is the sultan who is protected by the command of God, and they are the people of polytheism. It appears - and God knows best - that what Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, and Ad-Dahhak meant by this is that the angels’ guard over the servant is similar to the guards of these people over their kings and princes. Imam Abu Jaafar bin Jarir narrated here a very strange hadith. He said: Al-Muthanna told me, Ibrahim bin Abdul Salam bin Saleh Al-Qushayri told us, Ali bin Jarir told us, on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Abdul Hamid bin Jaafar, on the authority of Kinanah Al-Adawi, who said: Uthman bin Affan entered upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, tell me about the servant, how many angels are with him? He said: “An angel is on your right hand over your good deeds, and he is the commander over the one on the left. If you do a good deed, ten are written down, and if you do a bad deed, the one on the left will say to the one on the right: Write it down?” He said: No, perhaps he will seek forgiveness from God and repent, so he will ask His permission three times. When he says it three times, He will say: Write it down, may God relieve us of him. What a bad companion he is! How little he watches God and how little he is ashamed of us. God says: Not a word does he utter but there is a watcher by him ready to record it. And two angels before you and behind you. God the Most High says: He has guardians before him and behind him (al-An’am 2:17). And an angel holding your forelock, so if you humble yourself before God, He will raise you up, and if you are arrogant towards God, He will break you. And two angels on your lips, and they do not preserve for you anything except the prayers upon Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And an angel standing over your mouth, not allowing a snake to enter your mouth, and two angels over your eyes. So these are ten angels over every human being. The angels of the night descend upon the angels of the day, because the angels of the night are in addition to the angels of the day. So these are twenty.” A king over every human being, and Satan during the day and his son at night. Imam Ahmad may God have mercy on him said: Aswad bin Aamer told us, Sufyan told us, Mansour told me, on the authority of Salim bin Abi Al-Jaad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: There is not one of you but has a companion from the jinn and a companion from the angels assigned to him. They said: And you, O Messenger of God? He said: And me, but God has helped me against him, so he only commands me to do good. Muslim alone transmitted it. And his statement: They protect him from the command of God. It was said that what is meant is their protecting him from the command of God. It was narrated by Ali bin Abi Talhah and others on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and this is the view of Mujahid, Saeed bin Jubair, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i and others. Qatada said: They protect him by the command of God. He said: In some readings, they protect him by the command of God. Ka’b al-Ahbar said: If every easy and every difficult situation were revealed to the son of Adam, he would see everything as devils. Had God not assigned angels to you to defend you in your food, drink, and private parts, then you would have been snatched away. Abu Umamah said: There is no human being who has an angel with him to defend him until he hands him over to what was destined for him. Abu Majlaz said: A man from Murad came to Ali may God be pleased with him while he was praying and said: Beware, for some people from Murad want to kill you. He said: With every man are two angels who protect him from what was not destined. So when the destiny comes, they leave him alone with it. Indeed, the appointed time is a secure paradise. Some of them said, They protect it from the command of God by the command of God, as it came in the hadith that they said: O Messenger of God, what do you think of the incantations that we recite, do they repel anything from the decree of God? He said, They are from the decree of God. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashja told us, Hafs bin Ghiyath told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Jahm, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: God revealed to a prophet from the prophets of the Children of Israel: Tell your al-Nas 114:There is no one from the people of a village or household who are obedient to God and then turn from it to disobeying God, except that God will turn from them what they love to what they hate. Then he said: Verifying that is in the Book of God: Indeed, God will not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves. This was mentioned in a hadith with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), as Al-Hafiz Muhammad bin Uthman bin Abi Shaybah said in his book Sifat Al-Arsh: Al-Hasan bin Ali told us, Al-Haitham bin Al-Ash’ath Al-Salami told us, Abu Hanifa Al-Yamani Al-Ansari told us on the authority of Umair bin Abdul Malik, who said: Ali bin Abi Talib delivered a sermon to us on the pulpit of Kufa. He said: Whenever I stopped talking to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), he would begin with me, and whenever I asked him about something, he would tell me. And he told me on the authority of his Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, who said: “The Lord said: By My glory and majesty and My elevation above My throne, there is no village or household that was upon what I disliked of disobedience to Me and then turned from it to what I loved of obedience to Me, except that I turned for them from what they disliked of My punishment to what they love of My mercy.” This is strange, and in its chain of transmission is someone I do not know.

13:12: God the Almighty informs us that He is the One who makes the lightning subservient, which is the bright light that is seen shining through the clouds. Ibn Jarir narrated that Ibn Abbas wrote to Abu al-Jild asking him about lightning, and he said: Lightning is water. And His statement: in fear and hope Qatada said: Fear for the traveler who fears its harm and hardship, and hope for the resident who hopes for its blessing and benefit and hopes for God's provision, and creates the heavy clouds meaning He creates them as new creations, and due to their abundant water they are heavy and close to the ground. Mujahid said: The heavy clouds contain water. He said: And the thunder glorifies Him with praise like His statement: And there is not a thing but glorifies Him with praise. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid told us, Ibrahim bin Saad told us, my father told me: I was sitting next to Humaid bin Abdul Rahman in the mosque, and an old man from Banu Ghaffar passed by, so Humaid sent for him. When he came, he said: O son of my brother, make room for me and you, for he was a companion of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So he came and sat between me and him, and Humaid said to him: What is the hadith that you narrated to me from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? The old man said to him: I heard from an old man from Banu Ghaffar that he heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: God creates the clouds, and they speak the most beautiful speech and laugh the most beautiful laugh. What is meant - and God knows best - is that their speech is thunder and their laughter is lightning. Musa bin Ubaidah said on the authority of Saad bin Ibrahim, who said: God sends rain, and there is none more funny than him, nor more pleasant to speak than him, so his laughter is lightning and his speech is thunder. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Hisham bin Ubaidullah Al-Razi told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Muslim, who said: It has reached us that lightning is an angel with four faces: the face of a human, the face of a bull, the face of an eagle, and the face of a lion. When it strikes with its tail, that is lightning. Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Abdul Wahid bin Ziyad told us, Al-Hajjaj told us, Abu Matar told us, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of his father, who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard thunder and lightning, he would say: O God, do not kill us with Your wrath, and do not destroy us with Your punishment, and pardon us before that. It was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Bukhari in the Book of Etiquette, and Al-Nasa’i in Al-Yawm wa Al-Laylah, and Al-Hakim in his Mustadrak from the hadith of Al-Hajjaj bin Artah, on the authority of Abu Matar, but he did not name him. Imam Abu Jaafar bin Jarir said: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Israel told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that whenever he heard thunder, he would say: Glory be to Him whom the thunder glorifies with His praise. It was narrated on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, that whenever he heard the sound of thunder, he would say: Glory be to Him whom it glorifies. It was also narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Tawus, and Al-Aswad bin Yazid, that they would say that. Al-Awza’i said: Ibn Abi Zakariya would say: Whoever says when he hears thunder: Glory be to God and His praise, will not be struck by lightning. It was narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr that whenever he heard thunder, he would stop talking and say: Glory be to Him whom the thunder glorifies with His praise, and the angels do so out of fear of Him, and he would say: This is indeed a severe threat to the people of the earth. Narrated by Malik in his Muwatta’ and by Al-Bukhari in the Book of Etiquette. Imam Ahmad said: Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Tayalisi told us, Sadaqah ibn Musa told us, Muhammad ibn Was’ told us, on the authority of Shatir ibn Nahar, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Your Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, said: If My servants obeyed Me, I would have given them rain at night, made the sun rise upon them during the day, and made them hear the sound of thunder.” Al-Tabarani said: Zakariya bin Yahya Al-Saji told us, Abu Kamil Al-Jahdari told us, Yahya bin Katheer Abu Al-Nadr told us, Abdul Karim told us, Ata told us on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you hear thunder, remember God, for it does not strike one who remembers. And the Almighty’s statement: And He sends down thunderbolts and strikes with them whom He wills, meaning He sends them as a punishment with which He takes revenge on whomever He wills. That is why they will increase in frequency at the end of time, as Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad bin Mus’ab told us, ‘Amara told us on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Abu Sa’eed Al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Thunderbolts will increase in frequency when the Hour approaches until a man comes to the people and says: Who struck you this morning? They will say: So-and-so, so-and-so, and so-and-so struck.” It was narrated about the reason for its revelation what was narrated by Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la Al-Mawsili: Ishaq told us, Ali bin Abi Sarah Al-Shaibani told us, Thabit told us on the authority of Anas that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, once sent a man to a man from the Pharaohs of the Arabs, and said: Go and call him for me. He said: So he went to him and said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, calls you. So he said to him: Who is the Messenger of God, and what is God? Is he of gold, or of silver, or of copper? He said: So he returned to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him. He said: O Messenger of God, I have told you that he is more stubborn than that. He said such and such to me. He said to me: Go back to him a second time. So he went and said the same to him. So he returned to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, I have told you that he is more stubborn than that. He said: Go back to him and call him. So he returned to him a third time. He said: So he repeated that statement to him. While he was speaking to him, God Almighty sent a cloud in front of his head, and it thundered and a thunderbolt fell from it, and it blew off the skull of his head. Then God Almighty revealed: And He sends down thunderbolts. Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Ali ibn Abi Sarah. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar narrated it on the authority of Abdah bin Abdullah on the authority of Yazid bin Harun, on the authority of Daylam bin Ghazwan, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas, and he mentioned something similar, and he said: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, Affan told us, Abaan bin Yazid told us, Abu Imran Al-Joni told us on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Sahar Al-Abdi that he was informed that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent him to a tyrant to call him and said: Have you seen your Lord? Is He gold? Or is He silver? Or is He pearl? He said: While he was arguing with them, God sent a cloud that thundered, so He sent a thunderbolt upon him, and it took the skull of his head, and this verse was revealed. Abu Bakr bin Ayyash said on the authority of Laith bin Abi Salim, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: A Jew came and said: O Muhammad, tell me about your Lord, what is He made of? Is He made of copper, or of pearls or rubies? He said: A thunderbolt came and took him, and God revealed the verse: And He sends down thunderbolts. Qatada said: It was mentioned to us that a man denied the Qur’an and belied the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so God sent a thunderbolt that destroyed him, and God revealed the verse And He sends thunderbolts, and they mentioned the reason for its revelation the story of Aamer bin At-Tufayl and Arbad bin Rabi’ah, when they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Medina and asked him to give them half of the matter, but the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, refused them, so Aamer bin At-Tufayl - may God curse him - said to him: By God, I will fill it against you with pure horses and strong men, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: God forbids that from you and the sons of Qaylah, meaning the Ansar. Then they were about to kill the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so one of them spoke to him, and the other drew his sword to kill him from behind, but God Almighty protected him from them and preserved him, so they left Medina and set out among the Arab tribes, gathering people to fight him, may God bless him and grant him peace, so God sent a cloud containing thunderbolts upon Arbad and burned him, and as for Aamer bin Al-Tufail, so God sent the plague upon him, and a great swelling appeared in him, and he kept saying: O family of Amer, a swelling like the swelling of a virgin, and death in the house of Saluliya, until they died, may God curse them, and God revealed in a similar matter: And He sends thunderbolts and strikes with them whom He wills while they dispute about God, and in that Labid bin Rabi’ah, brother of Arbad, said in his eulogy: I fear death for Arbad, but I do not fear the star of the fish or the lion Thunder and lightning struck me with the loss of the knight on the day of the calamity of Najd Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Mas`adah ibn Sa`id al-`Attar told us, Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir al-Hizami told us, `Abd al-`Aziz ibn `Imran told me, `Abd al-Rahman and `Abdullah ibn Zayd ibn Aslam told me on the authority of their father, on the authority of `Ata` ibn Yasar, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas that Arbad ibn Qays ibn Juza` ibn Jalayd ibn Ja`far ibn Kilab and `Amir ibn al-Tufayl ibn Malik came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in Madinah. They went to him while he was sitting and sat in front of him. `Amir ibn al-Tufayl said: O Muhammad, what will you give me if I become Muslim? Give me the wool and you the mud. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No. When they returned from him, Amer said: By God, I will fill it with horses and men against you. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: May God protect you. When Arbad and Amer left, Amer said: “O Arbad, I will distract Muhammad from you with talk, so strike him with the sword, for if you kill Muhammad, the people will not do more than accept blood money and hate war, so we will give them blood money.” Arbad said: I will do so. So they came back to him, and Aamer said: O Muhammad, get up with me so I can talk to you. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, got up with him and they sat against the wall, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood with him talking to him. Aamer said: Who is this, O Sa`d? He said: This is Asid bin Hudhair Al-Kataib, so they went out until they were at Al-Raqam, then God sent a thunderbolt upon Arbad and killed him, and Aamer went out until he was at Al-Kharam, God sent a wound that took him, and night overtook him in the house of a woman from Banu Salul, so he began to touch his wound in a circle and say: A gland like a camel’s gland in the house of a Salul woman, she wishes that he would die in her house, then he mounted his horse and brought him until he died on it returning, so God revealed about them: “God knows what every female bears and what the wombs absorb and what they gain, and everything with Him is by measure. Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Great, the Exalted. Whether among you is he who conceals his speech or declares it aloud, and he who is hidden by night and goes forth by day. He has guardians before him and behind him who guard him by the command of God. Indeed, God does not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves. And when God intends evil for a people, there is no repelling it, and they have no protector besides Him.” He said: The guardians by the command of God guard Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, then he mentioned Arbad and what he was killed by. He said, And He sends down thunderbolts and the verse. And His statement, And they dispute about God, meaning they doubt His greatness and that there is no god but Him, and He is severe in penalty. Ibn Jarir said: Severe in what He has decreed as punishment for those who transgress against Him, are rebellious and persist in their disbelief. This verse is similar to His statement, “And they planned a plan, and We planned a plan, while they perceived not. So see how was the end of their plan - that We destroyed them and their people, all together.” And on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, and He is severe in penalty, meaning severe in taking. And Mujahid said: severe in strength.
13:13: God the Almighty informs us that He is the One who makes the lightning subservient, which is the bright light that is seen shining through the clouds. Ibn Jarir narrated that Ibn Abbas wrote to Abu al-Jild asking him about lightning, and he said: Lightning is water. And His statement: in fear and hope Qatada said: Fear for the traveler who fears its harm and hardship, and hope for the resident who hopes for its blessing and benefit and hopes for God's provision, and creates the heavy clouds meaning He creates them as new creations, and due to their abundant water they are heavy and close to the ground. Mujahid said: The heavy clouds contain water. He said: And the thunder glorifies Him with praise like His statement: And there is not a thing but glorifies Him with praise. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid told us, Ibrahim bin Saad told us, my father told me: I was sitting next to Humaid bin Abdul Rahman in the mosque, and an old man from Banu Ghaffar passed by, so Humaid sent for him. When he came, he said: O son of my brother, make room for me and you, for he was a companion of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So he came and sat between me and him, and Humaid said to him: What is the hadith that you narrated to me from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? The old man said to him: I heard from an old man from Banu Ghaffar that he heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: God creates the clouds, and they speak the most beautiful speech and laugh the most beautiful laugh. What is meant - and God knows best - is that their speech is thunder and their laughter is lightning. Musa bin Ubaidah said on the authority of Saad bin Ibrahim, who said: God sends rain, and there is none more funny than him, nor more pleasant to speak than him, so his laughter is lightning and his speech is thunder. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Hisham bin Ubaidullah Al-Razi told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Muslim, who said: It has reached us that lightning is an angel with four faces: the face of a human, the face of a bull, the face of an eagle, and the face of a lion. When it strikes with its tail, that is lightning. Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Abdul Wahid bin Ziyad told us, Al-Hajjaj told us, Abu Matar told us, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of his father, who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard thunder and lightning, he would say: O God, do not kill us with Your wrath, and do not destroy us with Your punishment, and pardon us before that. Imam Abu Jaafar bin Jarir said: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Israel told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that whenever he heard thunder, he would say: Glory be to Him whom the thunder glorifies with His praise. It was narrated on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, that whenever he heard the sound of thunder, he would say: Glory be to Him whom it glorifies. It was also narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Tawus, and Al-Aswad bin Yazid, that they would say that. Al-Awza’i said: Ibn Abi Zakariya would say: Whoever says when he hears thunder: Glory be to God and His praise, will not be struck by lightning. It was narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr that whenever he heard thunder, he would stop talking and say: Glory be to Him whom the thunder glorifies with His praise, and the angels do so out of fear of Him, and he would say: This is indeed a severe threat to the people of the earth. Narrated by Malik in his Muwatta’ and by Al-Bukhari in the Book of Etiquette. Imam Ahmad said: Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Tayalisi told us, Sadaqah ibn Musa told us, Muhammad ibn Was’ told us, on the authority of Shatir ibn Nahar, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Your Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, said: If My servants obeyed Me, I would have given them rain at night, made the sun rise upon them during the day, and made them hear the sound of thunder.” Al-Tabarani said: Zakariya bin Yahya Al-Saji told us, Abu Kamil Al-Jahdari told us, Yahya bin Katheer Abu Al-Nadr told us, Abdul Karim told us, Ata told us on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you hear thunder, remember God, for it does not strike one who remembers. 13:14: Ali ibn Abi Talib may God be pleased with him said, His is the call to truth. He said: Monotheism, narrated by Ibn Jarir. Ibn Abbas, Qatadah and Malik said on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, His is the call to truth, there is no god but God. And those they invoke besides Him, the verse, meaning, the example of those who worship gods other than God, is like one who stretches out his hands toward water to reach his mouth. Ali ibn Abi Talib said: Like one who takes water from the edge of a well with his hand, but he can never reach it with his hand, so how can he reach his mouth? Mujahid said, like one who stretches out his hands, he calls for water with his tongue and points to it, but it never comes to him. It was said: What is meant is like one who grasps his hand for water, for he cannot control anything from it, as the poet said: I and you are longing for you like someone who holds water but his fingers have not given him water. The other said: So, because of the love that was between us, I became like someone holding water in his hand. The meaning of this statement is that the one who extends his hand to the water is either holding it or reaching for it from a distance, just as he does not benefit from the water that has not reached his mouth, which made it a place for drinking. Likewise, these polytheists who worship a god other than God with Him will never benefit from them in this world or in the hereafter. For this reason, He said, And the supplication of the disbelievers is only in error.
13:15: The Almighty tells of His greatness and power, that He has subdued everything, and that everything is submissive to Him, and for this reason everything prostrates to Him willingly, from the believers and unwillingly from the disbelievers. And their shadows in the mornings meaning the early morning and the evenings which is the plural of asil, which is the end of the day, like the Almighty’s saying: Have they not seen what God has created of things that seek shade in their shadows? The verse.
13:16: The Almighty decides that there is no god but Him, because they acknowledge that He is the One who created the heavens and the earth, and He is their Lord and Manager, and yet they have taken guardians besides Him whom they worship, and those gods do not possess for themselves or for their worshippers, a fortiori, any benefit or harm, meaning that they do not obtain any benefit nor do they ward off any harm from them. So is the one who worships these gods equal to God, and the one who worships God alone, with no partner for Him, and is in light from his Lord? And for this reason He said: “Say: Are the blind and the seeing equal? Or are darkness and light equal? Or have they attributed to God partners who created like His creation so that the creation became similar to them?” That is, did these polytheists make gods with God who are similar to the Lord and resemble Him in creation, so they created like His creation so that the creation became similar to them, so that they do not know that it was created by a creation other than Him? That is, the matter is not like that, for nothing resembles Him, nor is He comparable to Him, nor does He have a peer, nor a counterpart, nor a minister, nor a son, nor a companion, God is far above that. Rather, these polytheists worshipped gods with Him, and they acknowledged that they were created by Him, His slaves, as they used to say in their Talbiyah: Here I am, You have no partner, except a partner who is Yours, You own him and what he owns, and as God Almighty informed us about them in His statement: We worship them only that they may bring us nearer to God. So God Almighty denounced them for believing that, and God Almighty does not allow anyone to intercede with Him except with His permission. And intercession does not benefit with Him except for one whom He permits. “And how many an angel is there in the heavens?” The verse, and He said: Indeed, every one of them has a partner. Who is there in the heavens and the earth but will come to the Most Merciful as a servant? He has enumerated them and counted them precisely. And all of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone.” So if all were servants, then they did not worship each other without proof or evidence, but rather merely out of opinion, invention and innovation. Then He sent His messengers from the first of them to the last of them, warning them against that and forbidding them from worshipping anyone other than God, but they denied them and disobeyed them, so the word of punishment was inevitably due to them. And your Lord does not wrong anyone.
13:17: This noble verse includes two examples of truth in its steadfastness and permanence, and falsehood in its decay and annihilation. God Almighty said: He sent down water from the sky meaning rain and the valleys flowed according to their capacity meaning each valley took according to its capacity, so this one is large and holds a lot of water, and this one is small and holds according to its capacity, and it is an indication of the hearts and their differences, some of them hold a lot of knowledge, and some of them do not hold a lot of knowledge, but rather are too narrow for it and the flood carried a rising foam meaning so there came on the surface of the water that flowed in these valleys a rising foam on it, this is an example. And His saying: And from that which they kindle in the fire, seeking ornaments or goods the verse, this is the second example, which is what is melted in the fire of gold or silver seeking ornaments, that is, to make ornaments of copper or iron, and it is made into goods, then foam rises from it as foam rises from that Thus does God set forth the truth and falsehood that is, when they come together, falsehood has no stability or permanence, just as foam does not remain with water or with gold and silver, and the like of them that are melted in the fire, rather it goes away and vanishes, and for this reason He said: As for the foam, it vanishes as scum that is, it is not benefited from, rather it disperses and is torn apart, and goes to the sides of the valley, and sticks to the trees, and the winds blow it away, and likewise the dross of gold, silver, iron, and copper, it vanishes and nothing returns from it and nothing remains except water, and that gold and the like are benefited from, and for this reason He said: And as for that which benefits people, it remains on the earth. Likewise does God set forth examples, like His saying, the Most High: And these examples We set forth for the people, and they do not “None will understand it except those of knowledge. Some of the predecessors said: If I read, for example, from the Qur’an and did not understand it, I would cry over myself, because God Almighty says: None will understand it except those of knowledge. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the words of God Almighty: He sends down water from the sky, and valleys flow according to their capacity, the verse, this is a parable that God has given, from which hearts bear according to their certainty and doubt. As for doubt, action is of no benefit with it, but as for certainty, God benefits its people with it, and it is His saying: As for the foam, which is doubt, it vanishes as cast-off, but as for that which benefits people, it remains on the earth, which is certainty. Just as jewelry is placed in the fire, its pure part is taken and its impurity is left in the fire, so God accepts certainty and leaves doubt. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: He sends down water from the sky, and valleys flow according to their capacity, and the flood carries a swelling foam, meaning: the flood carries what is in the valley of wood and dung, and from that which they kindle in the fire, which is gold, silver, jewelry, goods, copper, and iron. Copper and iron have impurity, so God made its impurity like the foam of water. As for that which benefits people, it is gold and silver, and as for that which It benefits the earth, so whatever it drinks of water produces vegetation. This is like the righteous deed that remains for its people, and the evil deed disappears from its people, just as this foam disappears. Likewise, guidance and truth came from God, so whoever acts according to truth, it will be for him and will remain, just as what benefits people on earth remains. Likewise, iron cannot be used to make a knife or sword until it is put in the fire, so its impurity is consumed, and its goodness is brought out and people benefit from it. Likewise, falsehood disappears. So when the Day of Resurrection comes and people are raised and deeds are presented, falsehood will deviate and perish, and the people of truth will benefit from the truth. This is how it was narrated in its interpretation from Mujahid, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Ata’, Qatadah, and more than one of the predecessors and successors. And God, the Most High, gave two examples for the hypocrites at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah 2:one of fire and one of water. They are His saying, Their example is that of one who kindled a fire, but when it illuminated what was around him 2:17. Then He said, Or like a rainstorm from the sky in which is darkness and thunder and lightning 2:17. And likewise He gave two examples for the disbelievers in Surat An-Nur 2:17. The first is His saying, And those who disbelieved - their deeds are like a mirage 2:17. A mirage only occurs in intense heat, and for this reason it is stated in the two Sahihs: The Jews will be asked on the Day of Resurrection, What do you want? They will say, O our Lord, we are thirsty, so give us something to drink. It will be said, Will you not return? They will return to the Fire, but it will be like a mirage, its parts crushing each other. Then the Almighty said in the other parable: Or like darknesses in a deep sea Al-Bukhari and Muslim and in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abu Musa Al-Ash’ari, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The example of what God has sent me with of guidance and knowledge is like the example of rain falling on a land. Some of it accepted the water and produced abundant grass and herbs, and some of it was barren and held the water, so God benefited the people with it, so they drank, pastured, watered, and planted. And some of it fell on another group, and it was nothing but lowlands that neither held water nor produced grass. That is the example of one who understood the religion of God and God benefited him with what He sent me with and benefited with it, so he learned and taught, and the example of one who did not raise his head with that and did not accept the guidance of God with which I was sent.” This is an aquatic example. And he said in the other hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurayrah told us, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “My example and yours is like that of a man who kindled a fire. When it illuminated what was around him, the moths and these insects that fall into the fire began to fall into it. He tried to hold them back, but they overcame him and rushed into it. He said: So that is my example and yours.
