It was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim from the hadith of Ismail bin Ayyash, on the authority of Artah bin Al-Mundhir, on the authority of Abu Al-Hajjaj Yusuf Al-Ilahani, who said: I heard Abu Umamah and he mentioned something similar. It was mentioned in the hadith that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to visit the graves of the martyrs at the beginning of each year and say to them: “Peace be upon you for what you have endured. What an excellent final home!” And so did Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman.
13:24: God Almighty says, informing about those who have these praiseworthy qualities that they will have the best outcome in this world and the hereafter: Those who fulfill the covenant of God and do not break the contract and they are not like the hypocrites who, when one of them makes a covenant, betrays it, when he quarrels, lies, and when he is entrusted, betrays it. And those who maintain what God has ordered to be maintained of maintaining family ties, doing good to them, to the poor and needy, and doing good deeds. And fear their Lord that is, in what they do and what they leave of deeds, and they observe God in that, and they fear the evil of the reckoning in the hereafter. For this reason, He commanded them to be upright and righteous in all their movements and stillness, and all their limited and transgressive states. And those who are patient, seeking the countenance of their Lord that is, from forbidden things and sins, so they weaned themselves from them for the sake of God Almighty, seeking His pleasure and abundant reward. And establish prayer. “And spend from what We have provided for them,” that is, on those for whom it is obligatory to spend, such as wives, relatives, and strangers, the poor, needy, and destitute, secretly and publicly, that is, in secret and in public, and no situation prevents them from that, during the night and the ends of the day. And they repel evil with good, that is, they repel evil with good. So if someone harms them, they respond with kindness, patience, tolerance, forgiveness, and pardon, as God Almighty says: “Repel evil with that which is better, and then he between whom and you there was enmity will become as though he was a devoted friend. And none is granted it except those who are patient, and none is granted it except one having great good fortune.” For this reason, He said, informing about these happy people who are characterized by these good qualities, that they will have the final abode, then He explained that by saying: Gardens of Eden, and Eden is the abode, that is, gardens of abode in which they will remain forever. And on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, he said: There is a palace in Paradise called Eden, around which are towers and meadows, in which there is…” Five thousand doors, on each door five thousand ink marks, none shall enter it except a prophet, a friend, or a martyr. Ad-Dahhak said about His statement: Gardens of Eden: The city of Paradise, in which are the messengers, prophets, martyrs, and imams of guidance, and the people are around them and the gardens are around them, both narrated by Ibn Jarir. And His statement: And whoever is righteous among their fathers, spouses, and offspring means He will gather them with their beloved ones in it from among the fathers, family, and children, from among the believers who are righteous to enter Paradise, so that their eyes may be comforted by them, so that the degree of the lower one is raised to the degree of the higher, as a favor from God and a favor, without diminishing the degree of the higher one, as God Almighty said: And those who believe and whose offspring follow them in faith - We will join with them their offspring Al-An’am 2:17. And His statement, “And the angels will enter upon them from every gate. Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured. And excellent is the final home.” That is, the angels will enter upon them from here and there to congratulate them on entering Paradise. So when they enter it, the angels will come to them as Muslims, congratulating them for what they have received from God of closeness, favor, and residence in the House of Peace in the company of the truthful, the prophets, and the noble messengers. Imam Ahmad, may God have mercy on him, said: Abu Abd al-Rahman told us, Saeed ibn Abi Ayoub told me, Maruf ibn Suwaid al-Harrani told us, on the authority of Abu Ashana al-Ma’afari, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-’As, may God be pleased with them both, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Do you know who will be the first of God’s creation to enter Paradise? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: “The first of God’s creation to enter Paradise will be the poor emigrants who fill the gaps and protect against hardships. One of them will die with a need in his chest that he cannot fulfill. God Almighty will say to whomever He wills of His angels: ‘Go to them and greet them.’ The angels will say: ‘We are the inhabitants of Your heaven and the best of Your creation. Do You command us to go to these people and greet them?’ He will say: ‘They were servants who worshipped Me and did not associate anything with Me.’ The gaps will be filled and hardships will be protected. One of them will die with a need in his chest that he cannot fulfill. He said: ‘Then the angels will come to them at that time and enter upon them from every gate: ‘Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured. Excellent is the final home.’” Narrated by Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani on the authority of Ahmad ibn Rushdin, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Salih, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Wahb, on the authority of Amr ibn al-Harith, on the authority of Abu Ashana. He heard Abdullah ibn Amr on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The first group to enter Paradise will be the poor emigrants who are protected from hardships, and when they are commanded, they listen and obey. If a man among them has a need for a ruler, it will not be fulfilled until he dies with it in his chest. And God will call Paradise on the Day of Resurrection, and it will come with its adornments and decorations, and He will say: Where are My servants who fought in My cause, and were harmed in My cause, and struggled in My cause? Enter Paradise without punishment or reckoning. And the angels will come and prostrate themselves and say: Our Lord, we glorify You with praise night and day, and we sanctify You. Who are these whom You have preferred over us? The Lord, the Almighty, will say: These are My servants who struggled in My cause and were harmed in My cause. Then the angels will enter upon them from every gate: ‘Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured. Excellent is the final home.’” Abdullah bin Mubarak said on the authority of Baqiyyah bin Al-Waleed: Artah bin Al-Mundhir told us, I heard a man from the elders of the army called Abu Al-Hajjaj say: I sat with Abu Umamah and he said: When a believer enters Paradise, he will be reclining on his couch, and with him are two rows of servants, and at the edge of the rows is a gated door. An angel will come and ask permission, and the one next to him will say to the one next to him, An angel is asking permission, until he reaches the believer and he says, Give permission. The one closest to the believer will say, Give him permission, and the one next to him will say to the one next to him, Give him permission, until he reaches the furthest one at the door, and it will be opened for him, so he enters and greets the Prophet, then he leaves. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. It was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim from the hadith of Ismail bin Ayyash, on the authority of Artah bin Al-Mundhir, on the authority of Abu Al-Hajjaj Yusuf Al-Ilahani, who said: I heard Abu Umamah and he mentioned something similar. It was mentioned in the hadith that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to visit the graves of the martyrs at the beginning of each year and say to them: “Peace be upon you for what you have endured. What an excellent final home!” And so did Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman.
13:25: This is the state of the wretched and their characteristics, and the mention of what they will have in the Hereafter, and their fate will be different from what the believers will have, just as they were characterized by characteristics different from their characteristics in this world. Those people used to fulfill their covenant with God and connect what God commanded to be connected, while these people break the covenant of God after its ratification and sever what God commanded to be connected and spread corruption on earth as proven in the hadith "The signs of the hypocrite are three: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks his promise, and when he is entrusted he betrays." In another narration And when he makes a covenant he betrays it and when he disputes he acts immorally. That is why He said Those people will have the curse which is being removed from mercy, and for them is an evil home which is an evil outcome and final destination, and their refuge is Hell, and an evil resting place it is. Abu Al-Aaliyah said about the Almighty’s saying: And those who break the covenant of God verse, he said: They are six characteristics of the hypocrites. If they are dominated by people, they show these characteristics: If they speak, they lie, if they promise, they break their promise, if they are entrusted, they betray, they break the covenant of God after ratifying it, they sever what God has commanded to be joined, and they spread corruption on earth. If they are dominated by people, they show three characteristics: If they speak, they lie, if they promise, they break their promise, and if they are entrusted, they betray.
13:26: The Almighty mentions that He is the One who expands provision for whomever He wills, and restricts it for whomever He wills, because of His wisdom and justice in that. These infidels rejoiced in what they were given of worldly life as a lure for them and a respite, as He said: Do they think that what We provide them with of wealth and children * We hasten for them in good things? Rather, they do not perceive. Then He belittled worldly life in comparison to what the Almighty has stored for His believing servants in the Hereafter, as He said: And what is the worldly life compared to the Hereafter except enjoyment, as He said: Say, ‘The enjoyment of this world is little, and the Hereafter is better for him who fears God, and you will not be wronged a thread.’ And He said: Rather, you prefer the worldly life * While the Hereafter is better and more lasting. Imam Ahmad said: Wakee’ and Yahya bin Saeed told us: Ismail bin Abi Khalid told us, on the authority of Qais, on the authority of Al-Mustaddir, the brother of Banu Fihr, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The world in comparison to the Hereafter is like what one of you puts this finger in the sea. So let him see what he brings back,” and he pointed with his index finger. Narrated by Muslim in his Saheeh. In another hadith, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by a dead skinny kid, and the skinny kid had small ears, and he said: By God, the world is more insignificant to God than this is to its people when they throw it away.
13:27: God Almighty tells us about what the polytheists said, Why not? meaning, Why did he not send down to him a sign from his Lord? like their saying, Then let him bring us a sign as the former ones were sent. This has been discussed more than once, and that God is able to answer what they asked for. In the hadith, God revealed to His Messenger when they asked Him to turn Safa into gold, to make a spring flow for them, and to move the mountains around Mecca, so that its place would become meadows and gardens: If you wish, O Muhammad, I will give them that, and if they disbelieve, I will punish them with a punishment that I have not punished anyone in the worlds with, and if you wish, I will open for them the door of repentance and mercy. He said: Rather, I will open for them the door of repentance and mercy. For this reason, He said to His Messenger: “Say: God misguides whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns back.” That is, He is the misguider and the guide, whether He sent the Messenger with a sign in accordance with what they suggested or did not answer their question, for guidance and misguidance are not dependent on that or its absence, as He said: And neither signs nor warnings avail a people who do not believe. And He said: Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has come into effect will not believe, even if every sign came to them until they see the painful punishment. And He said: “And even if We had sent down to them The angels and the dead spoke to them, and We gathered together before them everything before. They would not believe unless God willed, but most of them are ignorant. That is why He said: “Say: God misguides whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns back [to Him].” That is, He guides to Himself whoever turns back to God, returns to Him, seeks His help, and supplicates to Him. Those who have believed and whose hearts are assured by the remembrance of God. That is, they are content and rest in the side of God, and are at peace when remembering Him, and are satisfied with Him as a Master and Helper. That is why He said: Unquestionably, by the remembrance of God hearts are assured. That is, He is worthy of that. And His statement: Those who believe and do righteous deeds - for them is bliss and a good place of return. Ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Joy and delight. Ikrimah said: What a good thing for them. Ad-Dahhak said: Envy for them. Ibrahim An-Nakha’i said: Good for them. Qatada said: It is an Arabic word, a man says: Blessed are you, meaning you have found good. And he said in another narration: Blessed are they, “and a good place of return,” meaning a return. These statements are one thing, there is no contradiction between them. Saeed bin Jubair said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Blessed are they, he said: It is the land of Paradise in Abyssinian. Saeed bin Masjuh said: Blessed is the name of Paradise in Hindi. And this is how As-Suddi narrated on the authority of Ikrimah: Blessed are they is Paradise, and Mujahid said the same. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: When God created Paradise and finished with it, He said: Those who believe and do righteous deeds - for them is bliss and a good place of return, and that was when He was pleased. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hamid told us, Yaqub told us, on the authority of Ja`far, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, who said: Tuba is a tree in Paradise, every tree of Paradise is from it, its branches are beyond the wall of Paradise. This is how it was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, Ibn Abbas, Mughith ibn Sulayman, Abu Ishaq al-Sabi`i, and more than one of the Salaf, that Tuba is a tree in Paradise, in every house of it is a branch of it. Some of them mentioned that the Most Gracious, Blessed and Exalted, planted it with His hand from a pearl, and commanded it to spread, so it spread to wherever God, Blessed and Exalted, willed, and from its roots came forth springs of the rivers of Paradise of honey, wine, water, and milk. Abdullah ibn Wahb said: Amr ibn al-Harith told us that Diraaj Abu al-Samh told him on the authority of Abu al-Haytham, on the authority of Abu Sa`id al-Khudri, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, Tuba is a tree in Paradise, the distance of a hundred years, the clothes of the people of Paradise come out from its sleeves. Imam Ahmad said: Hasan bin Musa told us, I heard Abdullah bin Lahi’ah, Daraj Abu Al-Samh told us, that Abu Al-Haitham told him, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that a man said: O Messenger of God, blessed is he who saw you and believed in you. He said: Blessed is he who saw me and believed in me, and blessed, then blessed, then blessed is he who believed in me without seeing me. A man said to him: What is blessed? He said: “A tree in Paradise, the journey of which is a hundred years. The clothes of the people of Paradise emerge from its sleeves.” Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated on the authority of Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, on the authority of Mughirah al-Makhzumi, on the authority of Wahib, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Sahl ibn Sa`d, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: In Paradise there is a tree under whose shade a rider would travel for a hundred years without crossing it. He said: I told it to al-Nu`man ibn Abi `Ayyash al-Zarqi, who said: Abu Sa`id al-Khudri told me on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: In Paradise there is a tree under whose shade a rider would travel for a hundred years without crossing it. In Sahih Al-Bukhari, from the hadith of Yazid bin Zurai’, from Saeed, from Qatada, from Anas, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said regarding the words of God Almighty: and an extended shade, he said: In Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider would travel for a hundred years without crossing it. Imam Ahmad said: Surayj told us, Falih told us, from Hilal bin Ali, from Abd Al-Rahman bin Abi Amrah, from Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “In Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider would travel for a hundred years. Read if you wish, ‘and an extended shade.’” Both of them included it in the two Sahihs. In a wording also by Ahmad: Muhammad bin Ja’far and Hajjaj told us, they said: Shu’bah told us: I heard Abu Ad-Dahhak narrating from Abu Hurairah, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: In Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider would travel for seventy - or a hundred years - it is the tree of eternity. Muhammad bin Ishaq said on the authority of Yahya bin Ibad bin Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Asma bint Abi Bakr, may God be pleased with them both, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mention the Lote Tree of the Limit, and he said: A rider can travel in the shade of its branches for a hundred years - or he said - a hundred riders can find shade in its branches, and in it are beds of gold as if its fruit were jars. Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi. Ismail bin Ayyash said on the authority of Saeed bin Yusuf, on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, on the authority of Abu Salam al-Aswad, who said: I heard Abu Umamah al-Bahili say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is no one among you who enters Paradise except that he is taken to Tuba, and its sleeves are opened for him and he takes from it whatever he wants, if he wants white, if he wants red, if he wants yellow, and if he wants black like anemones, finer and more beautiful.” Imam Abu Jaafar bin Jarir said: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, Muhammad bin Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ash’ath bin Abdullah, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: Tuba is a tree in Paradise, and God says to it: Open for My servant whatever he wants, so it opens for him horses with their saddles and bridles, and camels with their reins, and whatever he wants of clothing. Ibn Jarir narrated a strange and amazing narration from Wahb ibn Munabbih here. Wahb, may God have mercy on him, said: In Paradise there is a tree called Tuba. A rider can travel in its shade for a hundred years without crossing it. Its flowers are ryat, its leaves are brocade, its branches are amber, its ground is ruby, its soil is camphor, and its mud is musk. From its roots flow rivers of wine, milk, and honey. It is a gathering place for the people of Paradise. While they are in their gathering place, angels from their Lord come to them, leading bridled camels with chains of gold. Their faces are like beautiful lamps, and their hair is like the silk of a marazi silk due to its softness. On them are saddles, their planks are ruby, their drums are gold, and their clothes are of fine silk and brocade. They dismount from it saying: Our Lord has sent us to you so that you may visit Him and greet Him. He said: They ride it, for it is faster than a bird, and softer than a moth, a noble race without a profession. A man walks beside his brother while he talks to him and whispers to him, and the ear of one riding animal does not reach the ear of the other, nor does the kneeling of one riding animal reach the kneeling of the other, to the point that the tree moves out of their way so as not to separate a man from his brother. He said: They come to the Most Gracious, Most Merciful, and He reveals His noble face to them so that they may look at Him. When they see Him, they say: O God, You are peace, and from You is peace, and majesty and honor are due to You. He said: Then the Most High says at that time: I am peace, and from Me is peace, and upon you is due My mercy and love. Welcome to My servants who feared Me in secret and obeyed My command. He said: They say: Our Lord, we did not worship You as You should be worshipped, and we did not value You as You should be valued, so give us permission to prostrate before You. He said: Then God will say: It is not a house of hardship or worship, but rather a house of kingship and bliss, and I have lifted from you the hardship of worship, so ask Me whatever you wish, for every man among you has a wish, so they will ask Him until the shortest of them wishes, so he will say: My Lord, the people of the world competed in their world and were distressed in it, my Lord, so give Me the equivalent of everything they had in it from the day I created it until the world ended, so God the Most High will say: Your wish fell short, and you asked for less than your status, this is for you from Me, and I will bestow upon you My status because there is no misery or shortcoming in My giving, He said: Then He will say: Show to My servants what did not reach their wishes, and did not cross their minds, He said: So they will be shown to them until their wishes that are in their souls fall short, and among what they will be shown to them will be two horned mules, on every four of them a bed of a single ruby, on every bed of it a dome of gold, hollowed out in every dome of it are furnishings from the furnishings of Paradise, and in every dome there will be two slave girls from the houris, on every slave girl Two of them are garments from the garments of Paradise, and there is no color in Paradise except that it is in them, and no scent or perfume except that it has perfumed them. The light of their faces penetrates the thickness of the dome until whoever sees them thinks that they are less than the dome. He sees their brains from above their legs like a white thread in a red ruby. They see for him a superiority over his companion like the superiority of the sun over stones or better, and he sees for them the same and enters to them and they greet him, kiss him, and cling to him, and say to him: By God, we did not think that God would create the likes of you. Then God Almighty commands the angels to walk with them in a row in Paradise until each man of them reaches the station that has been prepared for him. This hadith was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim with his chain of transmission on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih, and he added: So look at the gift of your Lord that He has given you, and behold, it is domes in the highest company, and rooms built of pearls and coral, their doors of gold, their beds of rubies, their furnishings of brocade and silk, and their pulpits of light gushing from their doors, and their platforms. A light like the sun's ray is like a shining star in the bright day, and lofty palaces in the highest heavens of rubies, their light shining, were it not subject to control, then the eyes would be dazzled. Whatever of those palaces is of white ruby, it is furnished with white silk, whatever is in them of red rubies, it is furnished with red brilliance, whatever is in them of green rubies, it is furnished with green brocade, and whatever is in them of yellow rubies, it is furnished with yellow purple, framed with green emerald, red gold, and white silver, its pillars and corners are of jewels, its honor is domes of pearls, and its towers are chambers of coral. So when they turned to what their Lord had given them, two mules of white ruby were brought near to them, the spirit blown into them, the immortal boys avoided them, in the hand of each of them was the wisdom of a mule from those mules, and its bridles and reins were of white silver strung with pearls and rubies, its saddles were adorned couches furnished with brocade and heavy silk, so they set off with them. Those mules were carried to the heart of the gardens of Paradise. When they reached their homes, they found the angels sitting on pulpits of light waiting for them to visit them, shake hands with them, and congratulate them on the honor of their Lord. When they entered their palaces, they found in them everything they had desired and wished for. At the door of each palace were four gardens: two gardens with branches, and two gardens with abundant rain. In them were two flowing springs, and in them were two pairs of every kind of fruit, and houris confined in pavilions. When they had settled in their homes and settled down, their Lord said to them: Have you found what your Lord promised to be true? They said: Yes, by our Lord. He said: Are you satisfied with the reward of your Lord? They said: Our Lord, we are satisfied, so be satisfied with us. He said: By My pleasure with you, you have entered My abode, and have looked upon My face, and My angels have shaken hands with you. So congratulations to you, an uninterrupted gift, in which there is no bitterness or resentment. Then they said: Praise be to God, who has removed sorrow from us, and admitted us to the abode of permanence by His grace, wherein no fatigue shall touch us, nor shall weariness touch us. Indeed, our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative. This is a strange context and an amazing trace, and some of it has supporting evidence. In the two Sahihs, it is stated that God Almighty says to that man who will be the last of the people of Paradise to enter Paradise: Wish, so he wishes, until when his wishes are over, God Almighty says: Wish for such and such, and wish for such and such, mentioning him, then He says: That is for you and ten times more like it. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Dharr, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the authority of God the Almighty, “O My servants, were the first of you and the last of you, the humans of you and the jinn of you, to stand on one plain and ask of Me, and I were to give everyone what he asked for, that would not decrease My kingdom in the slightest, any more than a needle decreases the sea if dipped in it.” The hadith in full. Khalid ibn Ma’dan said: In Paradise there is a tree called Tuba, which has udders, all of which will suckle the children of the people of Paradise. If a woman miscarries, she will be in one of the rivers of Paradise, rolling around in it until the Day of Resurrection, and she will be resurrected forty years old. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

13:30: God Almighty says: And just as We sent you, O Muhammad, to this nation, to recite to them what We have revealed to you, meaning to convey God's message to them, so We sent to the past nations that disbelieved in God, and the messengers before you denied them as an example, and just as We inflicted Our punishment and vengeance on those, so let these people beware of the vengeance that will befall them, for their denial of you is more severe than the denial of any other messenger. God Almighty says: By God, We have certainly sent to nations before you, and God Almighty says: "And messengers were denied before you, but they were patient over being denied and harmed until Our victory came to them. And there is no changing the words of God. And there has come to you some of the report of the messengers," meaning how We granted them victory and made the outcome for them and their followers in this world and the hereafter. And His statement: And they disbelieve in the Most Gracious means this nation among whom We sent you disbelieves in the Most Gracious and does not acknowledge Him, because they were averse to describing God as the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. That is why they refused on the day of Al-Hudaybiyah to write In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, and they said: We do not know what the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful is, as Qatadah said, and the hadith is in Sahih Al-Bukhari. And God the Most High said: “Say, ‘Call upon God or call upon the Most Gracious. Whichever [name] you call upon, to Him belong the best names.’” And in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Abdullah bin Omar, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The most beloved of names to God the Most High are ‘Abdullah’ and ‘Abdur-Rahman.’ “Say, ‘He is my Lord; there is no god except Him.’ That is, this is what you disbelieve in. I believe in Him, acknowledge Him, and admit His Lordship and Divinity. He is my Lord, there is no god except Him. In Him I have relied, that is, in all my affairs, and to Him I return, that is, to Him I turn, for no one deserves that except Him.
13:31: God Almighty says, praising the Qur’an that He revealed to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and preferring it over all the books revealed before it, And if there had been a Qur’an by which mountains could be moved, meaning if there had been a book in the previous books by which mountains could be moved from their places, or the earth could be split and split, or the dead could speak in their graves, then this Qur’an would have been the one described as such, and no other would have been, or it would have been more appropriate for it to be so because of the miracle in it, which man and the jinn, if they all gathered together, would not be able to produce anything like it, or even a surah like it. Despite this, these polytheists disbelieve in it and deny it. Rather, to God belongs the command entirely, meaning that all matters are referred back to God Almighty. Whatever God wills will be, and whatever He does not will will not be, and whomever God misguides, there is no guide for him, and whomever God guides, there is no misguider for him. The name Qur’an may be given to each of the previous books, because it is derived from all of them. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Hammam ibn Munabbih. He said: This is what Abu Hurairah told us, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Recitation was made easy for David, so he would order his mount to be saddled. He would recite the Qur’an before his mount was saddled, and he would not eat except from the work of his hands.” Al-Bukhari alone narrated it. What is meant by the Qur’an is the Psalms. And His statement, Have not those who have believed despaired? means that all creation would believe and know, or become clear, that if God had willed, He could have guided all of mankind? There is no proof or miracle more eloquent or effective for minds and souls than this Qur’an, which, if God had sent it down upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled and coming apart from fear of God. It is proven in Sahih that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is no prophet who was not given something that people believed in, but what I was given was a revelation that God revealed to me, so I hope that I will have the most followers on the Day of Resurrection.” This means that the miracle of every prophet was extinguished with his death, and this Qur’an is an everlasting proof, its wonders do not end, it does not become obsolete due to frequent repetition, and scholars do not get tired of it. It is the decisive factor, and it is not a joke. Whoever abandons it from a tyrant, God will break him, and whoever seeks guidance from other than it, God will lead him astray. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Munjab ibn al-Harith told us, Bishr ibn ‘Amara told us, ‘Umar ibn Hassan told us, on the authority of ‘Atiyyah al-‘Awfi, who said: I said to him: And if there were a Qur’an by which the mountains were moved (al-Baqarah 2:17), they said to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: If the mountains of Mecca were moved for us until they expanded so that we could plough therein, or if the land were cut up for us as Solomon used to cut up for his people by the wind, or if the dead were brought back to life as Jesus used to bring the dead back to life for his people, then God revealed this verse. He said: I said: Do you narrate this hadith from one of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace? He said: Yes, from Abu Sa’id from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn ‘Abbas, al-Sha’bi, Qatadah, al-Thawri and more than one other narrated this in the reason for the revelation of this verse, and God knows best. Qatadah said: If He had done this with a Qur’an other than yours, He would have done it with your Qur’an. And his saying, Rather, to God belongs the whole command. Ibn Abbas said: That is, He does not do of that except what He wills and He would not do it. It was narrated by Ibn Ishaq with his chain of transmission on his authority, and Ibn Jarir also said it. More than one of the early Muslims said about His saying, Have those who have believed not despaired?: Have those who have believed not known? And others read: Have those who have believed not become clear that if God willed, He could have guided all mankind? Abu Al-Aaliyah said: Those who have believed have despaired of being guided, and if God willed, He could have guided all mankind. And His saying, And those who disbelieve will not cease to be struck by a calamity because of what they have done, or it will descend near their homes. That is, because of their denial, calamities will not cease to strike them in this world or strike those around them, so that they may learn a lesson and take heed, as God the Almighty said, And We have certainly destroyed the towns around you and have repeated the signs that perhaps they will return. And He said, Do they not see that We come upon the land, reducing it from its borders? Are they then the victors? Qatadah said on the authority of Al-Hasan, or it will descend near their homes meaning the calamity. This is what is apparent from the context. Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Al-Mas'udi narrated to us from Qatada from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And those who disbelieve will continue to be struck by a calamity for what they have done, he said: a military expedition, or it will descend near their homes, Muhammad said: until the promise of God comes to pass, he said: the conquest of Mecca, and this is what Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and Mujahid said in one narration. Al-Awfi said from Ibn Abbas: A calamity will strike them for what they have done, he said: a punishment from the sky that will descend upon them, or it will descend near their homes, meaning the descent of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, upon them and his fighting them, and this is what Mujahid and Qatadah said. Ikrimah said in one narration from Ibn Abbas: A calamity, meaning a disaster. And all of them said: until the promise of God comes to pass, meaning the conquest of Mecca. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: the Day of Resurrection. And his statement: Indeed, God does not fail in His promise, meaning He will not break His promise to His messengers to support them and their followers in this world and the hereafter. "So do not think that God will fail to fulfill His promise to His messengers. Indeed, God is Exalted in Might and Owner of Retribution."
13:32: God Almighty says, comforting His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his denial of those of his people who denied him: And messengers before you were mocked, meaning you had an example in them, but I granted respite to those who disbelieved, meaning I granted them respite and gave them a reprieve, then I seized them, with a severe seizure. So how did you reach what you did to them, how you punished them, and how much respite you granted them, as God Almighty said: And how many a town did I grant respite to while it was wrongdoing? Then I seized it, and to Me is the final destination. And in the two Sahihs: Indeed, God grants respite to the wrongdoer until, when He seizes him, He does not let him escape. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: “And such is the seizure of your Lord when He seizes the towns while they are wrongdoers. Indeed, His seizure is painful and severe.”
13:33: God Almighty says: Is He who is in charge of every soul for what it has earned? That is, a Guardian, Knower, Watcher over every soul, He knows what the workers do of good and evil, and nothing is hidden from Him. And you are not engaged in any affair, nor do you recite from it any Qur'an, nor do you do any deed, but We are witnesses over you when you are engaged in it. God Almighty also says: And not a leaf falls but that He knows it. He also says: "And there is no creature on earth but that upon God is its provision, and He knows its place of dwelling and its place of storage. All is in a clear register." He also says: Whether among you is he who conceals his speech or declares it, and whether he conceals it by night or goes forth by day. He also says: He knows the secret and what is more hidden. He also says: And He is with you wherever you are, and God is Seeing of what you do. Is He like the idols that they worship, that neither hear nor see, nor reason, nor possess any benefit for themselves nor for their worshippers, nor remove harm from themselves nor from their worshippers? This answer was omitted because the context indicated it, which is His statement: And they have made for God partners, meaning they worshipped idols, rivals, and statues with Him. Say, ‘Name them,’ meaning inform us of them and reveal their identity so that they may be known, for they have no reality. For this reason He said: Or do you inform Him of something He does not know on the earth? meaning that it does not exist, because if it existed on the earth He would have known it, because nothing is hidden from Him. Or with an apparent statement, Mujahid said: with a conjecture of statement. Ad-Dahhak and Qatada said: With false speech, meaning that you worshipped these idols because you thought that they could benefit and harm, and you called them gods. “They are only names that you and your fathers have named, for which God has sent down no authority. They follow nothing but assumption and what their souls desire. And there has already come to them from their Lord guidance.” Rather, their plot has been made attractive to those who disbelieve. Mujahid said: Their statement, meaning what they are upon of misguidance and calling to it during the hours of the night and the ends of the day, like the saying of God the Almighty: And We have appointed for them companions who made [their] [right] seem attractive to them 3:10, and averted [people] from the path. Whoever reads it with the fat-ha on the sad, it means that when what they are upon was made attractive to them, and that it is the truth, they called to it, and they averted people from following the path of the Messengers. Whoever reads it with the damma, it means that because of what was made attractive to them of the correctness of what they are upon, they averted people from the path of God. For this reason, He said: And he whom God sends astray, for him there is no guide, just as He said: And he whom God desires to test, you will not possess for him anything from God. And He said: If you are eager for their guidance, then indeed God does not guide whom He wills. They go astray, and they have no helpers.
13:34: The Almighty mentioned the punishment of the disbelievers and the reward of the righteous, so He said after informing about the state of the polytheists and what they are upon of disbelief and polytheism, For them is a punishment in the life of this world, meaning at the hands of the believers, killing and captivity, And the punishment of the Hereafter, meaning that which is stored up with this disgrace in this world, is much more severe, meaning much more severe than this, as the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to those who cursed: The punishment of this world is lighter than the punishment of the Hereafter, and it is as he said, may God bless him and grant him peace, for the punishment of this world has an end, and that is eternal forever in a fire that is seventy times greater than this, and a bond whose density and severity cannot be imagined, as God the Almighty said: On that Day no one will punish with His punishment, and no one will bind with His bond, and God the Almighty said: “And We have prepared for those who deny the Hour a Blaze. When they see them from a distant place, they will hear its wrath and sighing. And when they are thrown therein into a narrow place chained together, they will cry out there, ‘Destruction.’ Do not cry out today, ‘Destruction.’” One and they claim much destruction. Say, Is that better or the eternal Garden which the righteous have been promised? It will be their reward and their destination. This is why He coupled this with His statement, The description and description of Paradise which the righteous have been promised is that rivers flow beneath it, meaning they are free in its corners and sides, and wherever its people wish, they can make it flow freely, meaning they can use it as they wish and wherever they wish, like His statement, "The description of Paradise which the righteous have been promised is that there are rivers of water unpolluted, rivers of milk whose taste never changes, rivers of wine delicious to those who drink, and rivers of pure honey. And for them therein are all kinds of fruits and forgiveness." And his saying: Its food is permanent and its shade is eternal meaning that in it are fruits, foods and drinks that never cease or perish. And in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Ibn Abbas regarding the eclipse prayer, in which it says: They said: O Messenger of God, we saw you eating something in this place of yours, then we saw you curdling, so he said: I saw Paradise - or I was shown Paradise - and I took a bunch of grapes from it, and if I had taken it, you would have eaten from it as long as the world remained. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya`la said: Abu Khaithama told us, `Abdullah bin Ja`far told us, `Ubaydullah told us, Abu `Aqil told us, on the authority of Jabir, who said: While we were praying the noon prayer, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came forward, so we came forward. Then he reached for something to take it, then he stepped back. When he had finished the prayer, Ubayy bin Ka`b said to him: O Messenger of God, today you did something in the prayer that we have never seen you do. He said: “Paradise and all that is in it of flowers and freshness were shown to me, and I reached for a bunch of grapes to bring them to you, but I was prevented from it. If I brought them to you, everyone between the sky and the earth would eat from them without any decrease in them.” Muslim narrated from the hadith of Abu al-Zubayr on the authority of Jabir, supporting some of it, and from `Utbah bin `Abd al-Salami that a Bedouin asked the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about Paradise, and he said: Are there grapes in it? He said: Yes. He said: How big is the bunch? He said: A month’s journey for the speckled crow, and it does not stop. Narrated by Imam Ahmad. At-Tabarani said: Muadh ibn al-Muthanna told us, Ali ibn al-Madini told us, Rayhan ibn Saeed told us, on the authority of Ibad ibn Mansur, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, on the authority of Abu Asma’, on the authority of Thawban, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If a man takes a fruit from Paradise, another one will take its place. Jabir ibn Abdullah said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The people of Paradise will eat and drink, but they will not blow their noses, defecate, or urinate. Their food will be belching like the scent of musk, and they will be inspired to glorify and sanctify God just as they are inspired to breathe.” Narrated by Muslim. Imam Ahmad and An-Nasa’i narrated from the hadith of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Tamam ibn Uqbah, who said: I heard Zaid ibn Arqam say: A man from the People of the Book came and said: O Abu Al-Qasim, do you claim that the people of Paradise will eat and drink? He said: Yes, by the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, a man among them will be given the strength of a hundred men in eating, drinking, sexual intercourse, and desire. He said: The one who eats and drinks will have a need, and there will be no harm in Paradise? He said: One of them will have a need that will be a secretion that will flow from their skin like the scent of musk, and his stomach will shrink. Narrated by Imam Ahmad and Al-Nasa’i. Al-Hasan bin Arafa said: Khalaf bin Khalifa told us on the authority of Hamid Al-Araj, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: You look at the bird in Paradise, and it falls before you roasted. It was mentioned in some hadiths that when it is finished, it returns to being a bird as it was, by God’s permission. God Almighty said: And abundant fruit, neither cut off nor forbidden. And He said: And its shades are low for them, and its fruits are made accessible. Likewise, its shade does not disappear or shrink, as God Almighty said: “And those who believe and do righteous deeds - We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide forever. They will have therein purified spouses, and We will admit them to a deep shade.” It was mentioned in the two Sahihs from more than one source that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Indeed, in Paradise there is a tree under whose shade a fast, diligent rider will travel for a hundred years without crossing it. Then he recited: and an extended shade. God, the Most High, often links the description of Paradise with the description of Hell to encourage people to enter Paradise and warn them against Hell. For this reason, when He mentioned the description of Paradise as He mentioned, He said after that: That is the reward of those who fear God, and the reward of the disbelievers is the Fire. God, the Most High, also said: “The companions of the Fire and the companions of Paradise are not equal. The companions of Paradise are the successful.” Bilal ibn Sa’d, the preacher of Damascus, said in one of his sermons: Servants of God, has an informant come to you to tell you that some of your worship has been accepted from you, or that some of your sins have been forgiven you? Do you think that We created you in vain and that you will not be returned to Us? By God, if the reward were to be hastened for you in this world, you would all belittle what was required of you. Or would you desire to obey God in order to hasten your worldly life and not compete for Paradise whose food is eternal? Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

13:36: God Almighty says: And those to whom We have given the Scripture and they are based on it rejoice in what has been revealed to you that is, from the Qur'an, because of the evidence in their books of its truthfulness and good tidings, as God Almighty said: Those to whom We have given the Scripture recite it with its true recitation the verse, and God Almighty said: "Say, 'Believe in it or do not believe. Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it, when it is recited to them, fall upon their faces in prostration * And say, 'Glory be to our Lord! The promise of our Lord has surely been fulfilled'" that is, if what God promised us in our books of sending Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is true and will inevitably be fulfilled and will happen, then glory be to Him, how true is His promise, to Him alone is praise and they fall upon their faces weeping, and it increases them in humility, and His statement: And among the parties are those who deny some of it that is, among the groups are those who deny some of what has been revealed to you. Mujahid said, And among the parties meaning the Jews and Christians, are those who deny some of it meaning some of the truth that came to you. Qatada and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said the same. This is like what God Almighty said: And indeed, among the People of the Scripture is he who believes in God the verse, Say, ‘I have only been commanded to worship God and not to associate anything with Him’ meaning, I was only sent to worship God alone, with no partner for Him, just as the prophets before me were sent. To Him I invite meaning, to His path I invite people, and to Him is my return meaning, my return and destiny. And His statement: And thus We have sent it down as an Arabic judgment meaning, just as We sent the messengers before you, and sent down to them the books from the heaven, thus We have sent down to you the Qur’an as a perfect and Arabic judgment. We have honored you with it, and preferred you over all others with this clear, evident, and manifest Book, “which falsehood cannot approach from before it or from behind it: it is sent down by One Who is Wise, Praiseworthy.” And His statement: And if you were to follow their desires meaning their opinions after what has come to you of knowledge meaning from God, the Most High, you would have against God neither a protector nor a helper. This is a warning to the people of knowledge not to follow the paths of the people of misguidance after they have come to it from following the Prophetic Sunnah and the Muhammadan path, upon the one who brought it, may the best prayers and peace be upon him who brought it.

13:38: God the Almighty says: Just as We sent you, O Muhammad, as a human messenger, so We sent the messengers before you as human beings who ate food, walked in the markets, came to wives, and had children, and We made for them wives and children. God the Almighty said to the most honorable and final of the messengers: Say, ‘I am only a human being like you, to whom revelation is sent.’ In the two Sahihs, it is narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “As for me, I fast and break my fast, I stand and sleep, I eat meat, and I marry women. Whoever turns away from my way is not of me.” Imam Ahmad said: Yazid told us, Al-Hajjaj bin Artah told us, on the authority of Makhul, who said: Abu Ayyub said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Four are from the ways of the messengers: using perfume, marriage, using the siwak, and using henna.” Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Sufyan bin Wakee’ on the authority of Hafs bin Ghayath, on the authority of Al-Hajjaj, on the authority of Makhul, on the authority of Abu Al-Shamal, on the authority of Abu Ayoub, and he mentioned it, then he said: This is more authentic than the hadith in which Abu Al-Shamal was not mentioned. And His saying: And it is not for a Messenger to bring a sign except by permission of God meaning he would not bring his people a miracle unless he was given permission to do so. That is not up to him, but up to God, the Almighty, He does what He wills and decrees what He wants. For every term there is a book meaning for every appointed period, a book written in it, and everything with Him is measured. “Do you not know that God knows what is in the heaven and the earth? Indeed, that is in a book. Indeed, that, for God, is easy.” Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim used to say regarding His saying: For every term there is a book meaning for every book there is a term, meaning for every book that He sent down from the heaven there is a set period with God, and a specific amount, so for this reason God erases what He wills of it, and confirms meaning until it was all abrogated by the Qur’an that God sent down to His Messenger, may the prayers and peace of God be upon him. And His saying God erases what He wills and confirms the commentators differed regarding that. Al-Thawri, Waki’, and Hisham said on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Al-Munhal bin Amr, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr! On the authority of Ibn Abbas: He manages the affairs of the year, and God erases whatever He wills except misery and happiness, life and death. In another narration: God erases whatever He wills and confirms. He said: Everything except death, life, misery and happiness, for He has finished with them. Mujahid said, God erases whatever He wills and confirms, except for life, death, misery, and happiness, for they do not change. Mansour said, “I asked Mujahid, saying, ‘Have you seen the supplication of one of us who says, ‘O God, if my name is among the happy ones, then confirm it among them, and if it is among the miserable ones, then erase it from them and make it among the happy ones?’” He said: Good. Then I met him after that, a year or more later, and I asked him about that, and he said: Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night the two verses. He said: He decrees on the Night of Decree what will be in the year of provision or calamity, then He advances what He wills and delays what He wills. As for the Book of happiness and misery, it is fixed and does not change. Al-A’mash said, on the authority of Abu Wa’il Shaqiq ibn Salamah: He often used to supplicate with this supplication: O God, if You have written us as miserable, then erase it and write us as happy, and if You have written us as happy, then confirm us, for You erase what You will and confirm, and with You is the Mother of the Book. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Ibn Jarir also said: Amr ibn Ali told us, Muadh ibn Hisham told us, my father told us, on the authority of Abu Hakimah Asmah, on the authority of Abu Uthman al-Nahdi, that Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said while he was circumambulating the House and crying: O God, if You have written for me misery or a sin, then erase it, for You erase what You will and confirm, and with You is the Mother of the Book, so make it happiness and forgiveness. Hammad said on the authority of Khalid Al-Hadha’, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with him, that he also used to supplicate with this supplication. Sharik narrated it on the authority of Hilal bin Hamid, on the authority of Abdullah bin Ukaim, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, similarly. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna told me, Hajjaj told us, Khassaf told us, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Ibrahim, that Ka’b said to Umar bin Al-Khattab: O Commander of the Faithful, were it not for a verse in the Book of God, I would have informed you of what will happen until the Day of Resurrection. He said: What is it? He said: The statement of God Almighty: God erases what He wills verse, and the meaning of these statements is that God abrogates whatever He wills of the decrees, and confirms whatever He wills of them. This statement may be supported by what Imam Ahmad narrated: Waki’ told us, and Sufyan - he is al-Thawri - told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Isa, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi al-Ja’d, on the authority of Thawban, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A man is deprived of provision because of the sin he commits, and nothing repels the decree except supplication, and nothing increases lifespan except righteousness. Al-Nasa’i and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan al-Thawri with it. It is proven in Sahih that maintaining family ties increases one’s lifespan. In another hadith, Supplication and divine decree are swaying between the heaven and the earth. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Sahl ibn Askar told me, Abd al-Razzaq told us, Ibn Jarir told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “God has a Preserved Tablet, the length of five hundred years, made of white pearl, with two covers of ruby - and the two covers are two tablets - for God the Almighty, every day three hundred and sixty moments, He erases what He wills and confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book.” Al-Layth ibn Sa’d said, on the authority of Ziyadah ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi, on the authority of Fadala ibn Ubayd, on the authority of Abu al-Darda’, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The remembrance is opened in the three hours remaining of the night, in the first hour of which He looks at the remembrance in which no one else looks, and He erases what He wills and confirms. And he mentioned the rest of the hadith, narrated by Ibn Jarir. Al-Kalbi said: God erases whatever He wills and confirms. He said: He erases from the provision and increases it, and He erases from the life span and increases it. It was said to him: Who told you this? He said: Abu Salih, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah bin Riab, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then he was asked after that about this verse, and he said: He writes down all the speech until Thursday, then everything in which there is no reward or punishment is dropped from it, such as your saying: I ate and drank, I entered and left, and similar speech, and it is true, and He confirms what there is reward and upon it is punishment. Ikrimah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The Book is two books, a book from which God erases whatever He wills and confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: God blots out what He wills and confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book, he says: He is the man who spends his time in obedience to God, then returns to disobeying God, and dies in error, so he is the one who blots out, and the one who confirms is the man who works in disobedience to God, and he had previously done good until he dies in obedience to God, and he is the one who confirms. It was narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair that it means: He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, and God is over all things competent. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: God blots out what He wills and confirms, he says: He changes whatever He wills and abrogates it, and confirms whatever He wills and does not change it. And with Him is the Mother of the Book, and the sum of that with him in the Mother of the Book is the abrogator and the abrogated, and what is changed and what is confirmed, all of that is in a book. Qatada said regarding his statement: God blots out what He wills and confirms, like his statement: We do not abrogate a verse or cause it to be forgotten, the verse. Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: God erases what He wills and confirms, he said: The infidels of Quraysh said when the verse And it is not for a messenger to bring a sign except by God’s permission was revealed: We do not see Muhammad owning anything and he has finished with the matter, so this verse was revealed to frighten and threaten them, “If We wish, We can innovate for him from Our affair whatever We wish, and we innovate every Ramadan, so He erases what He wills and confirms what He wills of the people’s provisions and their calamities and what He gives them and what He allocates to them.” Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: God erases what He wills and confirms. He said: Whoever’s time has come, he goes, and whoever is alive, he continues to his time. Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him, chose this statement. His statement: And with Him is the Mother of the Book. He said: The lawful and the unlawful. Qatada said: That is, the entirety of the Book and its origin. Ad-Dahhak said: And with Him is the Mother of the Book. He said: A book with the Lord of the Worlds. Sunayd ibn Dawud said: Mu`tamir told me on the authority of his father, on the authority of Yasar, on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he asked Ka`b about the Mother of the Book, and he said: God knows what He is creating and what He created is doing. Then He said to His knowledge: Be a book, and it was a book. Ibn Jurayj said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And with Him is the Mother of the Book. He said: The Reminder.

13:40: God the Almighty says to His Messenger, And either We show you O Muhammad, some of the humiliation and punishment We promise your enemies in this world, or We cause you to die that is, before that, then upon you is only the message that is, We sent you to deliver God's message to them, and you have done what you were commanded to do, and upon Us is the reckoning that is, their reckoning and reward, as God the Almighty says: "So remind, for you are only a reminder. You are not a controller over them, except for he who turns away and disbelieves. Then God will punish him with the greatest punishment. Indeed, to Us is their return. Then indeed, upon Us is their reckoning", and His statement, Have they not seen that We come to the land, reducing it from its borders? Ibn Abbas said: Have they not seen that We open land after land for Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace? And he said in a narration: Have they not seen the town being destroyed until the population is in one area? Mujahid and Ikrimah said: We reduce it from its borders, he said: Its destruction. Al-Hasan and Ad-Dahhak said: It is the victory of the Muslims over the polytheists. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The decrease of its people and its blessings. Mujahid said: The decrease of souls and fruits and the destruction of the land. Al-Sha’bi said: If the land were decreasing, your house would be cramped for you, but souls and fruits are decreasing. And Ikrimah said the same: If the land were decreasing, you would not find a place to sit in, but it is death. And Ibn Abbas said in a narration: Its destruction is due to the death of its scholars, jurists and good people. And Mujahid also said the same: It is the death of scholars. In this meaning, Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir narrated in the biography of Ahmad Ibn Abdul Aziz Abu Al-Qasim Al-Masri Al-Wa’iz, who lived in Isfahan, Abu Muhammad Talha Ibn Asad Al-Marwi told us in Damascus, Abu Bakr Al-Ajri recited to us in Mecca, he said: Ahmad Ibn Ghazal recited to us on his own authority: The earth lives if its world lives. When a world dies, a part of it dies. Like the earth, it comes to life when rain falls on it, but if it refuses, destruction returns to its folds. The first statement is more appropriate, which is the emergence of Islam over polytheism, village after village, like His statement: And We destroyed the towns around you verse, and this is the choice of Ibn Jarir.

13:42: God the Almighty says: And those before them plotted against their messengers, and wanted to expel them from their country, so God plotted against them and made the outcome for the righteous, as He says: And when those who disbelieved plotted against you to confine you or kill you or expel you - and they plotted, and God planned - and God is the best of plotters, and God the Almighty says: "And they plotted a plot, and We plotted a plot, while they perceived not. * So see how was the end of their plot - that We destroyed them and their people, all together. * So those were their houses, desolate because of what they did wrong", the two verses. And His saying: He knows what every soul earns means that He the Almighty knows all secrets and consciences and He will reward every worker for his work And He will know the disbelievers, and the other reading is the disbelievers, For whom is the final home meaning for whom will the circle and outcome be or for the followers of the messengers, no, rather it is for the followers of the messengers in this world and the hereafter, and praise and thanks be to God.
13:43: God the Almighty says: These infidels belie you and say: You are not a messenger meaning God did not send you. "Say: God is sufficient as a witness between me and you" meaning God is sufficient for me. He is the witness over me and over you. He is a witness over me in what I conveyed of the message, and a witness over you, O deniers, in what you fabricate of slander. And His statement: And he who has knowledge of the Book It was said: It was revealed about Abdullah bin Salam, as Mujahid said. And this statement is strange, because this verse is Meccan, and Abdullah bin Salam only converted to Islam at the beginning of the Prophet's (peace be upon him) arrival in Medina. The most apparent in this is what Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: They are from the Jews and Christians. Qatadah said: Among them are Ibn Salam, Salman, Tamim Al-Dari, and Mujahid said in a narration on his authority: It is God the Almighty. Saeed bin Jubair denied that it meant Abdullah bin Salam and said: It is Meccan. He used to read it: And he who has knowledge of the Book and said: From God, and this is how Mujahid and Al-Hasan Al-Basri read it. Ibn Jarir narrated from the hadith of Harun al-A’war from al-Zuhri from Salim from Ibn Umar that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited it: And with Him is the knowledge of the Book, then he said: There is no basis for it in the hadith of al-Zuhri with the trustworthy ones. I said: Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la narrated it in his Musnad from the path of this Harun ibn Musa, from Sulayman ibn Arqam, and he is weak, from al-Zuhri from Salim from his father, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, and it is not proven, and God knows best. What is correct in this is that and with Him is a generic name that includes the scholars of the People of the Book who find the description and attributes of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in their previous books from the glad tidings of the prophets about him, as God the Almighty said: “And My mercy encompasses all things, so I will prescribe it for those who fear God and give zakah and those who believe in Our verses * Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered prophet, whom they find written down with them in the Torah and the Gospel” verse. And God the Almighty said: Was it not a sign to them that the scholars of the Children of Israel knew him verse, and similar things in which there is report about the scholars of the Children of Israel that they know that from Their revealed books. It was mentioned in the hadith of the scholars on the authority of Abdullah bin Salam that he converted to Islam in Mecca before the migration. Al-Hafiz Abu Naim Al-Isfahani said in the book Dala’il Al-Nubuwwah, which is an important book: Sulayman bin Ahmad Al-Tabarani told us, Abdun bin Ahmad told us, Muhammad bin Musaffa told us, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us on the authority of Muhammad bin Hamza Yusuf bin Abdullah bin Salam, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather Abdullah bin Salam, that he said to the Jewish rabbis: I wanted to narrate a festival in the mosque of our fathers Abraham and Ishmael, so he went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was in Mecca, and he met them after they had returned from Hajj, and he found the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Mina with people around him, so he stood with the people, and when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, looked at him, he said: Are you Abdullah bin Salam? I said: Yes, he said: Come closer. So I came closer to him. He said: I ask you by God, O Abdullah bin Salam, do you not find me in the Torah as the Messenger of God? Then I said to him: Describe our Lord. He said: Gabriel came and stood before the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said to him: “Say: He is God, the One. God, the Self-Sufficient,” to the end of it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited it to us, and Ibn Salam said: I bear witness that there is no god but God and that you are the Messenger of God. Then Ibn Salam returned to Medina, and concealed his Islam. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, migrated to Medina, I was on top of a palm tree of mine, pruning it, and I threw myself down. My mother said: You belong to God. If it had been Moses, son of Imran, you would not have thrown yourself down from the top of the palm tree. I said: By God, I am happier with the arrival of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, than Moses, son of Imran, when he was sent. This is a very strange hadith. The end of the interpretation of Surat Ar-Ra`d. Praise and thanks be to God.
